newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: New Afghan rulers bar Kabul women from offices.
newsitem.headline: New Afghan rulers bar Kabul women from offices.

text.p: Afghanistan's new Taleban rulers on Friday barred women in the capital Kabul from working in offices.
The official Kabul Radio quoted a Taleban high council decree as telling women not to attend their offices until further orders.
The broadcast, monitored in Pakistan, also asked the women in general to cover their faces with the traditional "hejab" veil when they were out of their homes.
The Taleban issued similar orders for women when it captured the western Afghan town of Herat a year ago, provoking protests.
Kabul Radio resumed broadcasting on Friday after it fell silent on Thursday night.

The Taleban militia, a one-time band of student vigilantes, captured Kabul during the early hours of Friday morning, ousting President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government and executing former president Najibullah and his brother Shahpur Ahmadzai.
